title: Throughput & Latency Synthesis — Per-model / Per-route dashboard prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, synthesis-first dashboard that surfaces throughput, latency, and token-level metrics for a single model or route. The intent is to make it fast for engineers and SREs to understand trade-offs (latency vs throughput vs cost) and to diagnose regressions without leaving the Console. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype, chart specs for engineering (SVG/Canvas considerations), interaction spec, and handoff assets (tokens, layer comps).
goals: Surface combined throughput+latency signals in a single view so users can correlate spikes quickly
Provide token-level visibility (prompt vs generation vs function call tokens) to connect cost to behavior
Make it easy to compare model versions or route variants (canary overlays) and identify regressions
Keep the canvas compact enough to embed as a per-route snapshot in summary lists and as a full page for deep dives
user_stories: As an SRE, I want a single-pane overview showing P50/P90/P99 latency with concurrent throughput so I can spot capacity issues
As an ML engineer, I want to overlay an A/B model rollout so I can see whether the new model increases token usage or latency
As a product engineer, I want a cost lens that estimates cost per request and per-1000 tokens so I can evaluate economic impact of prompts
As a console user, I want to click any spike to load microtraces for that time window and route to trace causes
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows combined view: dual-axis latency line chart + throughput histogram/area that align on the time axis
Chart specs include data schema (timestamps, route_id, model_version, tokens.{prompt,generation,tool}, latency_ms, requests) as CSV-like column names for engineering
Token waterfall visualization specified with stacked categories and toggle to normalize by requests or show absolute token counts
Canary/rollout overlay supports two series with translucent coloring, legend, and delta summary (avg latency, tokens-per-request, cost delta)
Interactions: hover tooltips with percentiles and token breakdown, brush-to-zoom, quick-snap to 1h/6h/24h/7d, and link-to-trace button present
Figma file with annotated components, spacing tokens, responsive behavior for embedding in summaries, and handoff tokens included
chart_specs: Synthesis Panel (top): Dual-axis time series. Left axis latency_ms lines: P50 (solid), P90 (dashed), P99 (dot). Right axis throughput: requests_per_minute as semi-transparent area. X-axis shared time. Window: 1h/6h/24h/7d presets.
Throughput Heatmap (middle-left): 24h x minute-granularity heatmap of requests per minute, scalable to 7d with day slices. Color scale: log-normalized with threshold banding to highlight bursts.

Token Waterfall (middle-right): Stacked bar per-minute showing prompt_tokens, generation_tokens, function_call_tokens. Optional normalization toggle to tokens/request. Bars compressed in summary view, fully expanded in details view.
Unit Economics Row (bottom-left): Area chart for estimated cost_per_1000_tokens and cost_per_request (smoothed 10m rolling). Secondary overlay: estimated GPU token-cost (from backend model profiles).
Microtraces Sparkline Grid (bottom-right): Small-multiple sparklines (6-12) showing recent sample latency microtraces for slowest requests. Click opens full trace in Trace Viewer.
Delta Summary Card: Floating card showing percentage change between two selected series or time ranges (latency P90, tokens/request, cost/request).
Annotations: Event pins on time axis (deploys, config changes, infra incidents) with hover detail and link to incident/PR.
Responsive behavior: In compact (list) mode, show Synthesis Panel condensed to P90 sparkline + throughput microbar + cost dot; full view restores all subcharts.
interactions: Hover: show combined tooltip with timestamp, P50/P90/P99 latency values, requests/min, and token breakdown percentages
Brush: select time range to zoom charts and populate microtrace samples within that window
Series compare: choose up to 2 model versions or route variants to overlay; show delta summary and highlight statistically significant changes
Drill-to-trace: 'Open traces' button on any spike sends a pre-filtered query to the Trace Viewer with time window +/- 30s
Export: CSV download for the visible time window; include raw counters and percentile approximations
Annotations: attach note to a timestamp (team-only) that propagates to runbook links and incident channels
design_notes: Prefer canvas rendering for heatmap and waterfall due to density; SVG acceptable for small-multiple sparklines
Color palette: accessibility-checked (WCAG AA) with colorblind-safe palette for primary series and translucent overlays for comparisons
Performance: backend should provide pre-aggregated tiles (1m, 5m, 1h) to avoid client-side heavy reductions
Placeholder states: zero-data, partial-data, and degraded-metrics (when percentile pipelines lag) must be handled with clear CTAs
Avoid showing raw GPU utilization in the main panel; surface that in a separate infra tab to keep focus on application-level metrics
